clue.text: Erstwhile Tory minister's derisive witticism about European Parliament

indicators.note: about tells us the joke goes round the parliament, one piece wrapped around the other

parts.note: to josh is to tease, and a josh is a teasing jibe

explanation.surface: A former Conservative minister makes a mocking quip about the European Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Keith Joseph was a Conservative cabinet minister under Heath and Thatcher. The 's on 'minister's' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Keith Joseph served in Thatcher's cabinet, so he is a former Tory minister by surname.

clue.text: Deviously seek advantage, indulging in banter about Conservative

indicators.note: about means the bantering word wraps itself around the party letter

parts.note: jokey means full of jokes, given to banter

explanation.surface: Someone joshing about a Tory while slyly angling for an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To jockey for position is to manoeuvre craftily for an advantage, so the verb fits the scheming sense.

clue.text: Desire maybe creates trembling, right churning within

indicators.note: within says the turned abbreviation sits inside the shaken-up word
trembling suggests letters shaken into a new order
churning here turns the two letters round, so they run backwards

explanation.surface: Longing produces a tremble, with something churning inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desire' is a capitalised trap: it is the tram in Tennessee Williams's play. 'trembling' gives SEETCAR, and 'churning' turns the right round before 'within' puts it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: The play A Streetcar Named Desire makes Desire an example of a tram, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Turning cheek, resolute person on spiritual path

indicators.note: Turning tells us to read the word for cheek backwards

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk, insolence
grim can mean stern and unyielding, as in grim determination

explanation.surface: A determined traveller on a sacred journey turning the other cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrim travels to a holy place, a journey along a spiritual path.

clue.text: Unblocked all right?

definitions.meaning: a road that is unblocked can be travelled along, open to traffic

explanation.surface: Is the road clear and the situation okay?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both open to traffic and tolerably good, two separate senses.

clue.text: What's in spore mud in the air could convey

definitions.text: What's in spore mud in the air could convey

indicators.note: could convey suggests the letters can be carried into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Something airborne in muddy spores is being carried about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could convey' rearranges the eleven letters of 'mud in the air'; the whole clue gestures at a plant's reproductive organ in spore-bearing plants.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the male sex organ of ferns, mosses and algae, the spore-bearing plants.

clue.text: Hospital person is jerk, fictional doctor taking wrong direction

parts.note: to surge is to move with a sudden jerk or rush

indicators.note: taking the wrong direction means the villain's name is read backwards

parts.note: Dr No is the villain of Ian Fleming's Bond novel

explanation.surface: A hospital worker lurches as a storybook doctor heads the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a doctor who operates, a hospital professional.

clue.text: Scot wanting English restraint reversed

indicators.note: reversed tells us to write the word for restraint backwards

parts.note: a curb is a check or restraint

explanation.surface: A Scotsman needs an English check turned back.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert the Bruce was the Scottish king who beat the English at Bannockburn; 'wanting' simply means needing the extra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert the Bruce, King of Scots, is a famous Scotsman, also a common Scottish surname.

clue.text: Being inadequate, was first to be qualified!

indicators.note: inadequate says the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: an entity is a being, a thing that exists
led means was in front, was first

explanation.surface: Despite being inadequate, someone came first and got qualified.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entitled means having a right or qualification to something.

clue.text: Group left enthralled by enchanting female

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive inside the enchantress's name

parts.note: Circe is the sorceress of the Odyssey who bewitched Odysseus's men

explanation.surface: A group of people left spellbound by a bewitching woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle is a set of people with shared interests, a social group.

clue.text: Romantic nonsense beginning to bind Germany and America

indicators.note: to bind means to hold the countries inside, wrapped around them

parts.note: start means beginning
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: Sentimental twaddle starts tying Germany and America together.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardust is a dreamy, romantic quality, a starry-eyed idealism.

clue.text: Odious old mob bumping off one of the bishops outside city

indicators.note: outside means these pieces go around the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: bumping off means removing one of the letters

parts.note: rabble is a disorderly mob
B is a chess notation for bishop, and the word has two
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A hateful old gang kills a bishop just outside town.
explanation.walkthrough: The mob word holds two bishops, so 'bumping off' removes just one; the City of London's postcode is the 'city'.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means extremely bad or detestable, a synonym of hateful.

clue.text: Broadcasting Lord coming to a party, one in company boasting

parts.note: Melvyn Bragg, Lord Bragg, is a long-standing BBC broadcaster
a do is a party

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the abbreviation for company

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A broadcasting peer turns up at a party, a member of the firm bragging.
explanation.walkthrough: Melvyn Bragg presents BBC radio and TV arts programmes and sits in the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: Braggadocio is boastful talk, empty swagger.

clue.text: Put up and put in having switched sides

indicators.note: switching sides here means changing left to right, a letter swap

parts.note: to elect is to vote into office, put in

explanation.surface: Something was raised and installed after changing allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'sides' are left and right: L becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect is to build or raise, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Al Capone in mob surprisingly convivial

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at an unexpected arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Gangster Al Capone turns out to be friendly among his mob.
explanation.definitionFit: Companionable means friendly and sociable, good company.

clue.text: Busy type meaning to get in the way — one held to be a bugbear

indicators.note: to get in the way means one piece pushes into the middle of another

parts.note: a bee is proverbially busy

indicators.note: held means the numeral is kept inside the word for meaning

parts.note: tenor is the general sense or meaning
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A busy person getting in the way is considered a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A bête noire is a pet hate, a thing one particularly dislikes.

clue.text: Super society with insufficient pounds for spending

indicators.note: for spending means a pound is used up, so that letter goes

parts.note: piffling means trivial, too small to matter
L stands for librae, pounds

explanation.surface: A wonderful club that hardly has any money to spend.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiffing is old-fashioned British slang for excellent, splendid.

clue.text: A fine notice from striker on gate, full of skill, about top governor

indicators.note: full of means the outer word holds the rest inside

parts.note: a picket is a striking worker standing at the factory gate

indicators.note: about means the word for skill goes round the ruler

parts.note: art is skill
a king is the top ruler

explanation.surface: A notice from a striker at the gate, mentioning a clever ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' is a worker on strike, not a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: A parking ticket is a written notice imposing a fine for illegal parking.

clue.text: One facing sun horribly sunburnt should be covered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: sunburnt skin is red

explanation.surface: Someone badly sunburnt from facing the sun ought to have cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Being insured means having cover under a policy.

clue.text: Position of ruler lacking good rapport

indicators.note: lacking means the letter is taken away

parts.note: kingship is the office or rank of a king

explanation.surface: A monarch's role without goodwill leaves little connection.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinship is a close bond or affinity, a sense of connection.

clue.text: Open country that's left in good shape

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the word for open country

parts.note: a heath is open uncultivated land

explanation.surface: Open land that has been left in fine condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in good health means being in good condition or fitness.

clue.text: Game — just four would get score

definitions.meaning: a handball game played in a court, like squash with hands
four of the number after four make twenty, a score

explanation.surface: A game where only four points would put you on the scoreboard.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, and four of them make twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Fives is a British court game in which the ball is struck with the hand; the plural of the number also works.

clue.text: Drink very little, all right? A day to be limited

parts.note: V, a single letter, is a tiny abbreviation for very

indicators.note: to be limited means the day is kept within the other letters

parts.note: OK means all right

explanation.surface: Have only a small drink, okay? A day of restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very little' means a shortened 'very': V. D sits between the O and K.
explanation.definitionFit: Vodka is a clear spirit, a type of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Authority and order at home, steps being taken to secure such

indicators.note: to secure means to hold the other pieces inside

parts.note: dance steps make a dance
OM is the Order of Merit
in means at home

explanation.surface: Power and discipline at home, with measures taken to ensure them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steps being taken' sounds like action, but steps here are dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominance is control or power over others, hence authority.

clue.text: Incidental charge about to be introduced

indicators.note: to be introduced means inserted into the word for charge

parts.note: to indict is to formally charge
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A minor charge that is about to be brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: Indirect costs or effects are secondary, not the main ones, much like incidental ones.

clue.text: Word of honour with which respected Indian is addressed by learners being keen

parts.words: Word of honour with which respected Indian is addressed
parts.note: Shri is an Indian honorific, like Mr
L is a learner driver's plate, so two learners give two Ls

explanation.surface: Students eagerly greet a respected Indian with a title of honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Word of honour' is not a promise here but an honorific title. 'keen' is the definition: a keen wind or note is piercing.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen can mean piercingly high-pitched, as in a keening wail, a sound that is sharp and piercing.

clue.text: Dud with aggro around? Yes and (hopefully!) no

definitions.text: Dud with aggro around? Yes and (hopefully!) no

indicators.note: around signals the letters are scattered about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Is it useless and aggressive? Aggressive yes, useless hopefully not.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the animal: it should be aggressive near intruders but hopefully not a dud.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch animal kept to protect property should be fierce and, ideally, effective.

clue.text: 'Have an accident' maybe in school lecture?

indicators.note: in means the euphemism goes inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: a child having an accident is wetting themselves, so to pee

explanation.surface: A child wetting themselves in school, maybe during a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' flags that 'have an accident' is a euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech is a formal talk to an audience, much like a lecture.
